Among 804 ARPI-experienced US mCRPC patients who started a line after an ARPI (Narayan et al., Clin Genitourin Cancer 2024;22(6):102188, doi:10.1016/j.clgc.2024.102188, Flatiron 2013 to 2022), that first post-ARPI line was enzalutamide in 239 (29.7%), abiraterone in 191 (23.8%) and docetaxel in 171 (21.3%), and 459 (57.1%) took a second ARPI. That cohort is the eligible pool above, patients starting a line after an ARPI, so a share of it is a share of each year's eligible patients. HLD-0915 is an oral once-daily androgen receptor-directed medicine built to work after ARPI resistance, so the place it is designed to take is the second ARPI, and 29.7% is the most any one medicine holds of this line.
